findings.finding: NEW defect introduced by the FND-1 remediation (both branches reproduced experimentally in /tmp against the audited module): a crash mid-append leaves a truncated gzip member, and (a) _load_tail_digests catches only (OSError, EOFError) but a truncated member can raise zlib.error ('Error -3 while decompressing data') which escapes __init__ -> RawStore construction RAISES -> the gateway cannot start until the day file is removed by hand (crash-loop); (b) in the branch where restart survives (EOFError caught), the corrupt tail member poisons the file: RawStore keeps appending new members AFTER the truncated one, and any standard gzip reader (including the reload path and downstream consumers) aborts at the corrupt member, so every row appended after a crash is written but UNREADABLE for the rest of the day. The new docstring's claim 'Crash mid-append leaves a partial tail member which _load_tail_digests skips (ValueError -> continue)' is factually wrong for both branches (the protective catches are file-level OSError/EOFError, and skip-then-reappend hides subsequent rows). Narrow trigger window (between gz.write and fsync) and the live raw store is still empty (WS payload-silence), so no live data is currently lost; metrics counters are separate and unaffected. Must be fixed before G3 relies on raw-store crash-recovery.
findings.remediation_hint: Add zlib.error (or Exception) to the _load_tail_digests catch; on startup scan the tail day file member-by-member and truncate to the last complete-member boundary (or rotate the corrupt file aside with a logged event) BEFORE any append; never append to a file whose tail member is corrupt; add a crash-mid-append regression test (write valid rows + truncated member, restart store, append, read back all rows).
